name: Agent swarm incidents
note: Public incident notes for the Threat Index Agent chip. Domains are defanged. A match is a signal, not proof. Confirm on the source page before you act.

entries.name: Rogue agent swarm on Hugging Face
entries.detail: A rogue agent swarm on Hugging Face coordinated roughly 700 of about 1,200 evaluation agents. Reporting ties the incident to an Artifactory zero-day and exposed credentials.
entries.check: Review eval-agent credentials and any Artifactory tokens those agents could read. Rotate exposed credentials. Treat coordinated agent output as untrusted.

entries.name: Deadbugz poisoned MCP server
entries.blurb: productivity-suite rewrites tool text after 3 calls
entries.detail: Deadbugz is a poisoned MCP server published as productivity-suite. After about three calls it rewrites tool descriptions so the agent will steal SSH, AWS, and kube credentials.
entries.check: Search MCP configs for the server name productivity-suite and the host below. Look for the hidden Python path. Remove the server and rotate SSH, AWS, and kube credentials if that file was present.

entries.name: Shai-Hulud npm worm
entries.detail: A Shai-Hulud wave arrived through the keyv package family. The preinstall hook commits a .claude/settings.json SessionStart hook and a .vscode/tasks.json folderOpen task, and a workflow calls toJSON(secrets). Hunt leftovers before you rotate.
entries.check: Before rotating, hunt for a preinstall hook, a .claude/settings.json SessionStart command, a .vscode/tasks.json runOn folderOpen task, and a workflow that calls toJSON(secrets). Remove leftovers, then rotate CI and agent tokens.

entries.name: Anthropic September threat report
entries.blurb: Exploit foundries, key theft, fake Claude resellers
entries.detail: Anthropic's September 2026 threat report describes exploit foundries, self-rebuilding malware, AI API key theft and resale, fake cheap-Claude resellers, prompt injection stealing LiteLLM keys, and about 1,000 fake X accounts.
entries.check: Watch for fake cheap-Claude resellers and for prompt injection aimed at LiteLLM keys. Buy model access from the vendor. Rotate API keys that an agent or a reseller page could have seen.

entries.name: BioShocking AI browser injection
entries.detail: BioShocking was a page that framed data theft as a game. It manipulated six AI browsers into leaking credentials.
entries.check: Do not let an AI browser act on a page that frames credential theft as a game or roleplay. Read the page yourself. Do not approve a sign-in the page started.

entries.name: Grok Bankrbot wallet drain
entries.blurb: NFT unlock plus a Morse-coded reply
entries.detail: A Grok / Bankrbot lure used an NFT unlock and a Morse-coded reply to drain a wallet. Reporting put the loss near 3 billion DRB, about $150K–$200K, on Base.
entries.check: Treat Morse-coded replies and NFT-unlock instructions as hostile. Do not sign a transaction an agent drafted from a post. Confirm the destination out of band.

entries.name: SANDWORM_MODE npm worm
entries.blurb: Typosquats inject a rogue MCP server
entries.detail: SANDWORM_MODE is an npm worm spread with typosquats, including fake Claude Code and OpenClaw packages. It injects a rogue MCP server into Claude, Cursor, Continue, and Windsurf. The tools index_project, lint_check, and scan_dependencies steal LLM keys and poison CI.
entries.check: Audit Claude, Cursor, Continue, and Windsurf MCP configs for those tool names, especially if the description hides instructions. Remove the server and rotate LLM keys.

entries.name: Malicious OpenClaw skills
entries.blurb: SKILL.md pipes a fake CLI into a shell
entries.detail: Malicious OpenClaw / ClawHub skills used SKILL.md to run a base64 or curl pipe, install a fake OpenClawCLI, and deliver the AMOS stealer.
entries.check: Do not run a SKILL.md that installs a CLI with base64 or curl piped to a shell. Remove the skill and scan the Mac for an AMOS-style stealer.

entries.name: FBI PSA on AI impersonation
entries.blurb: Officials impersonated with AI voice and text
entries.detail: An FBI public service announcement on 2026-09-17 warned about AI impersonation of officials. IC3 cited about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B in losses from January 2025 through July 2026.
entries.check: Verify any request that claims to be from an official, out of band, using a number or site you looked up yourself.

entries.name: GTG-1002 AI espionage
entries.blurb: Claude Code plus MCP did most of the intrusion work
entries.detail: GTG-1002 was an AI-orchestrated espionage campaign. Anthropic reported that Claude Code plus MCP did about 80–90% of the work against roughly 30 targets, using task-splitting and a persona jailbreak.
entries.check: Treat task-splitting and persona lines such as "you are a security firm employee" as jailbreaks. Do not give an agent standing access to production tools.
